description:
FILED s454ad (Opus round 12, agent AD), exposed when #755 removed the wild-
pathname abort that sat EARLIER in t/op/filetest.t; PRE-EXISTING (the base
tree emits the same form -- it just never got to run it).

    -f 'TEST';        # a whole statement: perl runs the filetest for its
                      # side effect (primes the `_` stat buffer)

t/op/filetest.t:159 is exactly this, priming `_` for line 160's
`is(-f _, 1, '_ is bareword after filetest operator')`.  PCL emits

    (p-- (p-scalar-ctx (pl-f "TEST")))

= unary minus of a call to user sub f -- "Undefined subroutine &main::f
called", which ABORTS the file's remaining forms (aborted-forms:1 in the
suite row; op/filetest.t currently 181/253).

The parenthesised and expression positions are fine; only the bare-statement
position mis-parses, so this is the #372/#476 filetest-at-statement-start
family (the statement path never hands `-f` to the filetest machinery).
Sibling on the next line: `sub _ { "this is not a file name" } is(-f _, ...)`
on ONE line is a counted DROP ("Missing case: Token::Magic<_> ...").

BAR: `-f 'TEST';` and `-e $f;` as void statements prime `_` (probe with a
following `-f _` read vs perl); op/filetest.t's aborted-forms goes 1 -> 0 and
rows 37-38 ("_ is bareword after filetest operator") return; re-splice the
snapshot row with the cause.
subject: `-f 'TEST';` as a VOID STATEMENT emits (p-- (pl-f "TEST")) -- a negated CALL to sub f; it is t/op/filetest.t's remaining aborted form
